question: to the Commission Catarina Martins (The Left) Subject:
Clearcutting in Ovar pine forest (Portugal) and the destruction of Priority Habitat 2270*

The Ovar forest perimeter is home to Priority Habitat 2270* (present condition: ‘unfavourable-poor’) and encompasses two special areas of conservation (SACs): PTCON0014 and PTCON0006. Since Ovar is designated as a ‘shaded area’ that falls within the scope of the Natura 2000 network, the Portuguese Nature Conservation and Forests Institute (ICNF) is enacting a forest management plan (2020-2038) without the need for a strategic environmental assessment (SEA). 363 hectares of mature pine forest are being cleared. These activities contravene the norms and practices of the ICNF, which has prohibited just such operations in a similar SAC in Mira (PTCON0055). In the light of the case law of the Court of Justice (judgments in Cases C-117/03, Dragaggi and C-244/05, Bund Naturschutz): 1.
Does the Commission deem Portugal to be in breach of its obligation to conserve the ‘shaded area’ in Ovar by authorising such destructive clearcutting?

By designating clearcutting as a ‘forestry operation’ that is exempt from an environmental impact assessment (EIA) and organising the project in such a way that plots of land are divided up into fewer than 10 hectares each, could these actions be construed as an attempt to obviate legal requirements designed to prevent the assessment of cumulative impacts, and hence be in breach of Directives 2001/42/EC and 2011/92/EU?

Will the Commission ascertain the facts of the matter and launch infringement proceedings against Portugal pursuant to Article 258 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU for breaches of Directives 2001/42/EC (SEA), 2001/92/EU (EIA) and 92/43/ECC (Habitats)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.8.2026) Priority Habitat 2270* is protected in 20 sites in Portugal, including near the Ovar region in the Special Area of Conservation (SAC) Ria de Aveiro (PTCON0061). Under Article 6(3) of the Habitats Directive1, any plan or project likely to have a significant effect on a Natura 2000 site must undergo an appropriate assessment, whether located inside or outside the site. National authorities may authorise such plans or projects only after establishing that they will not adversely affect the integrity of the site, without prejudice to Article 6(4) of the same Directive. Member States are responsible for ensuring that these requirements are complied with. Certain ‘forestry operation’ projects may fall under the scope of the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive2; however, there is no automatic obligation to carry out an environmental impact assessment. For such projects3, Member States must determine if an assessment is required, taking into account relevant selection criteria4. Forestry plans and programmes fall under the scope of the Strategic Environmental Assessment Directive5 and must be assessed, provided that certain conditions are fulfilled6. As stated in its Communication ‘EU Law: Better Results through Better Application’7, the Commission prioritises enforcement action in cases indicating a systematic breach of EU law in a Member State and considers national means of redress the most effective way to address individual alleged cases of non-compliance.
1 Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and

flora. OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, pp. 7–50. 2 Directive 2011/92/EU on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment, OJ L 26, 28.1.2011, as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU, OJ L 124, 25.4.2014 (EIA Directive). 3 Listed in Annex II, point 1(b) or (d) of the EIA Directive. 4 Such as project location (e.g. proximity to sensitive areas) and cumulation with other existing and/or approved projects. 5 Directive 2001/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 June 2001 on the assessment of the effects of certain plans and programmes on the environment, OJ L 197, 21.7.2001. 6 Plans and programmes prepared and/or adopted by a national, regional or local authority; required by legislative, regulatory or administrative provisions, and setting the framework for authorising projects listed in Annexes I and II to the EIA Directive or determined to require an appropriate assessment under the Birds (Directive 2009/147/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the conservation of wild birds, OJ L 20, 26.1.2010, p. 7–25) or Habitats Directives. 7 As set out in the Communication of 19 January 2017 (EU law: Better results through better application C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20) and in the Communication of 13 October 2022, COM(2022) 518 final - Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers.
